title: Aberrant cortical reorganization and astrogliosis underlie memory deficit post-traumatic brain injury: a longitudinal multiscale multimodal study
abstract: Integrating high-dimensional neuroimaging data across spatial scales remains a fundamental bottleneck in quantitative neuroscience. Here, we apply emerging analytical techniques including functional connectome gradient mapping and 3D segmentation of whole-brain cellular resolution microscopy data in a mouse model of traumatic brain injury. At the macroscale, longitudinal functional MRI revealed a transition from frontal hyperconnectivity to hippocampal hypoconnectivity and unimodal-transmodal gradient contraction indicating network dedifferentiation. At the cellular scale, deep-learning based segmentation of whole-brain light-sheet fluorescence microscopy volumes quantified regional astrogliosis, neuronal hyperactivity, and single-axon loss undetected by standard diffusion MRI. Multiscale multimodal data integration not only identified quantitative biomarkers predictive of memory performance post-injury but also enabled validation of in vivo modalities against more sensitive ex vivo histology. This study demonstrates a framework for probing complex multi-network cognitive functions and neurological disorders of network dysfunction.

title: Development of a deep learning model for glomerulus detection and segmentation in kidney histopathology images
abstract: Background: Estimation of nephron number, an indicator of renal reserve, requires quantitative assessment of glomerular number and size in kidney biopsy specimens. We aimed to develop an automated system for quantitative measurement of glomerular areas from clinical kidney biopsy images, across diverse kidney diseases. Methods: We developed a two-stage deep learning system combining Faster R-CNN for glomerular detection in whole-slide images (WSIs) and DeepLabV3+ for segmentation. Of 114 kidney biopsies (228 WSIs), 104 were used for model development and 10 for independent final evaluation. Agreement was assessed using the F1-score for detection, the Dice coefficient for segmentation, and the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) for glomerular area measurement. Analysis was performed at 40× total magnification (2.331 μm/pixel) and validated against 400× images. Results: In the independent evaluation set, the artificial intelligence (AI) model achieved a mean F1-score of 0.851 for detection, compared with 0.888 among experts. For segmentation, the Dice coefficient was 0.959 ± 0.011 and the per-pair ICC (2,1) for area measurement was 0.989 ± 0.009; both were comparable to inter-expert agreement. Bland–Altman analysis showed a mean bias of −344 μm 2 (95% limits of agreement, −1904 to 1216 μm 2 ) between 40× and 400× measurements. Conclusion: The two-stage model achieved glomerular segmentation and area measurement comparable to expert agreement in independent clinical data, with detection performance approaching inter-expert agreement, and provided reliable measurements at low magnification. This automated approach may facilitate large-scale quantitative kidney pathology and nephron number estimation from clinical kidney biopsies.

title: Ordinal Multi-Instance Learning for Automated Multi-Task Grading of Lumbar Degenerative Conditions on Sagittal MRI, with External Validation
abstract: Purpose: Lumbar spine MRI interpretation requires 25 structured severity judgments per examination (five degenerative conditions at five disc levels, each on a three-level ordinal scale), a time-consuming task with substantial inter-reader variability. We developed and externally validated a model that automates this complete scheme. Materials and Methods: A full-sequence multi-instance learning (MIL) model (ResNet34 backbone, bidirectional GRU, attention pooling over 24 uniformly sampled sagittal T2-weighted slices) with 25 cumulative-logit ordinal heads was trained on 1,204 examinations from the multi-institutional RSNA 2024 LumbarDISC dataset and internally validated on 213 held-out examinations. External validation used 60 retrospectively collected patients from an independent Chinese university hospital (four scanner vendors, radiology reports as the reference standard, no fine-tuning). Agreement was assessed with exact accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, McNemar tests, and patient-clustered bootstrap confidence intervals. Results: The ordinal model achieved 51.4% balanced accuracy internally (exact accuracy 65.1%), versus 16.3% for a single-slice baseline; severe-grade AUCs averaged 0.908 across conditions. Externally, it outperformed its softmax-weighted counterpart on exact accuracy (0.649 vs. 0.586; +6.3 percentage points, 95% CI +2.7 to +10.0) and sensitivity (0.868 vs. 0.833), with markedly fewer severe-grade false alarms (69 vs. 172 predicted severe cells; McNemar p<0.0001). Conclusion: A full-sequence MIL model with ordinal outputs automates the complete 25-task grading scheme on sagittal MRI and, in the first hospital external validation of such a model, reduced severe-grade over-prediction under domain shift without loss of sensitivity, supporting its role as a screening and triage aid.

title: ReSeg: Retraining-free segmentation of abdominal organs via generalizable semantic representation learning
abstract: Abdominal organ segmentation is essential in modern medical applications. While existing deep learning approaches demonstrate promising performance, their heavy reliance on large-scale image data raises concerns over generalization capability and privacy risks. This motivates the development of generalizable segmentation training paradigms based on domain-randomized image synthesis, facilitating generalization across unseen real image domains. However, existing paradigms either suffer from limited segmentation performance when applied to abdominal organs, or require dataset-specific finetuning. To address these limitations, we propose ReSeg, a novel two-stage retraining-free framework for domain-agnostic zero-shot abdominal organ segmentation. At the first stage, our organ-agnostic synthetic data-driven pretraining approach exploits semantically and visually diverse synthetic images generated by a dedicated data engine to optimize a Generalizable Semantic Representation Network (GSRNet). The network is thereby capable of learning semantic features robust against variations in anatomical structure, imaging contrast, resolution and spatial context, which provide universal representation capabilities that serve as a foundation for segmentation learning. Subsequently, in the second stage, we continue to train an Organ-specific Encoder-decoder Segmentation Network (OESNet), whose encoder is initialized with the pretrained weights. This training process is facilitated by another dedicated data engine, which generates diversified visual images while strictly retaining the inherent spatial layout of abdominal organs. Comprehensive evaluation on seven abdominal organ segmentation datasets across three different modalities including CT, MRI, and PET demonstrates that ReSeg consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods while eliminating the need for real training images.

title: From Canon to Nikon: Camera Domain Shift and Potential Equity Implications in Retinal AI
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy is a leading cause of preventable blindness, yet access to regular screening remains limited worldwide. AI offers a scalable approach, but its performance can be sensitive to image quality and acquisition conditions. In a Brazilian cohort of 8,524 patients, retinal images acquired with the Nikon NF5050 were more than twice as likely to have inadequate image quality compared with those acquired with the Canon CR-2, despite refurbished Canon systems costing more than twice as much as Nikon systems. This potential cost-quality trade-off highlights an important consideration for the reliability of AI systems deployed across heterogeneous imaging systems. Using a frozen pretrained retinal foundation model, we systematically evaluate whether camera-associated performance differences persist across 12 retinal disease classification tasks, four input resolutions, and five downstream classifiers. We find that camera-associated performance differences vary substantially across tasks, and that neither higher input resolution nor classifier choice consistently mitigates cross-camera variation. These findings identify camera platform as a potentially overlooked source of performance variability, with implications for the safety and reliability of retinal AI when deployed across heterogeneous imaging systems. We release all source code, evaluation scripts, and per-task results on GitHub to support reproducible benchmarking.

title: Two for One: Privileged Learning for Resource-Constrained Screening
abstract: Machine learning systems are often developed under data-rich conditions but deployed when only incomplete information is available. A natural example arises in colour fundus photography (CFP), where both eyes are commonly imaged because they can provide complementary information for ocular disease assessment. Prior approaches that exploit bilateral information either fuse both eyes in a single model or use knowledge distillation to compress a dual-eye teacher into a lightweight student that still requires both images at test time. However, bilateral acquisition may not always be feasible. We thus propose a privileged learning framework in which a teacher model has access to bilateral CFP images during training and learns representations informed by information from both eyes, while the student is trained to transfer this knowledge from the bilateral teacher using only a single-eye image as input. At inference, the student operates exclusively on this single-eye input and does not require the contralateral image. Experimental results show consistent improvements in area under the receiver operating characteristic curve over conventional monocular training, with the largest gains observed for left-eye images for the detection of age-related macular degeneration (0.931 vs. 0.966) and diabetic retinopathy (0.789 vs. 0.836).%, while requiring only a single-eye image at inference. By enabling models to benefit from bilateral information during training while requiring only a single-eye image at inference, our approach may support more reliable deployment in resource-constrained clinical and screening environments.

title: DGCM-SSFA: Dual-Granularity Cross-Modulation and Sparse Strip Frequency Attention for Efficient 3T-to-7T MRI Synthesis
abstract: Synthesizing high-fidelity 7T MRI from routinely acquired 3T scans offers a practical pathway to enhanced neuroimaging without the prohibitive cost of ultra-high-field scanners. While existing deep learning approaches have achieved promising results, state-of-the-art methods typically rely on either large-scale architectures exceeding 45 million parameters or computationally intensive ensemble strategies, limiting their practicality in resource-constrained clinical environments. In this work, we propose a compact multi-domain attention framework, termed DGCM-SSFA, that achieves competitive synthesis quality with only 11M parameters. The proposed architecture integrates two complementary modules into a U-Net Transformer backbone. First, a Dual-Granularity Cross-Modulated Feature Modulator (DGCM) is embedded at multiple hierarchical levels to enhance local edge and texture details through Sobel-guided spatial attention and depthwise frequency-aware channel attention with cross-branch gating. Second, a Sparse Strip Frequency Attention (SSFA) module at the bottleneck captures global spatial context via strip-pooled attention with near-linear complexity, while simultaneously performing FFT-based spectral modulation in the frequency domain. These two modules operate synergistically with the backbone's native channel attention, forming a triple-granularity feature refinement pipeline. Extensive experiments on the UNC and BNU 3T-to-7T MRI datasets across T1w and T2w modalities demonstrate that DGCM-SSFA achieves strong structural fidelity, attaining an SSIM of 0.8431 on BNU T2w---approaching the best benchmark value of 0.8624---and 0.8100 on BNU T1w, while using substantially fewer parameters than Transformer-based alternatives such as ResViT (123.4M) and FS-RWKV (45.4M).

In this work, we propose a compact multi-domain attention framework, termed DGCM-SSFA, that achieves competitive synthesis quality with only 11M parameters. The proposed architecture integrates two complementary modules into a U-Net Transformer backbone. First, a Dual-Granularity Cross-Modulated Feature Modulator (DGCM) is embedded at multiple hierarchical levels to enhance local edge and texture details through Sobel-guided spatial attention and depthwise frequency-aware channel attention with cross-branch gating. Second, a Sparse Strip Frequency Attention (SSFA) module at the bottleneck captures global spatial context via strip-pooled attention with near-linear complexity, while simultaneously performing FFT-based spectral modulation in the frequency domain. These two modules operate synergistically with the backbone's native channel attention, forming a triple-granularity feature refinement pipeline. Extensive experiments on the UNC and BNU 3T-to-7T MRI datasets across T1w and T2w modalities demonstrate that DGCM-SSFA achieves strong structural fidelity, attaining an SSIM of 0.8431 on BNU T2w---approaching the best benchmark value of 0.8624---and 0.8100 on BNU T1w, while using substantially fewer parameters than Transformer-based alternatives such as ResViT (123.4M) and FS-RWKV (45.4M).

title: Estimating Performance for Safe Deployment of Machine Learning Models
abstract: The main challenge in applying deep neural networks to real-world scenarios lies in distributional discrepancies between training and test datasets, often caused by variations in data acquisition conditions. Assessing the performance of pre-trained models without labels is crucial for safety, but this is complicated by deep models' overly optimistic probabilistic outputs, often exacerbated by class imbalances, leading to unreliable predictions. To address these issues, we introduce MOVAL, a novel MOdel eVALuation tool that estimates performance using unlabeled test data. MOVAL incorporates class-wise confidence calibration to adjust model outputs, allowing for the estimation of metrics beyond accuracy and mitigating the detrimental effects of class imbalance on confidence calibration. Additionally, we propose an ensemble approach that combines multiple calibrated confidence scores for a more robust solution. We validate MOVAL on natural and medical image datasets with various acquisition shifts, covering tasks from classification to segmentation. It achieves state-of-the-art results across evaluation metrics such as accuracy, F1-Score, AUC, and more. Furthermore, we demonstrate that MOVAL provides accurate performance estimations at the class, instance, and pixel levels, ensuring the transparent and safe deployment of machine learning models. We provide MOVAL as a deployment tool for monitoring and estimating performance under a range of domain shifts.

title: OpenMAP-HIE: Pathology Informed Score-based Diffusion Model for Unsupervised Neonatal Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy Lesion Segmentation
abstract: Accurate localization of neonatal hypoxic--ischemic encephalopathy (HIE) lesions on apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) images is clinically important but is limited by scarce expert annotations and substantial variation in lesion appearance. We propose OpenMAP-HIE, a pathology-informed score-based diffusion model for unsupervised HIE lesion localization without voxel-wise lesion supervision. A denoising diffusion model learns the healthy neonatal ADC distribution, while a ControlNet-based conditional branch preserves patient-specific anatomy. At inference, anomaly evidence is derived directly from differences between conditional and unconditioned noise predictions at independently evaluated diffusion noise levels, avoiding dependence on a final pseudo-healthy reconstruction or sequential reverse-diffusion chain. Based on the characteristic ADC reduction associated with acute HIE, only discrepancies consistent with the expected pathological direction are retained and aggregated across noise levels using a geometric mean. Spatial mean filtering further suppresses isolated responses. The framework was evaluated on the BONBID-HIE dataset. The ADC-only method achieved a Dice score of $0.283\pm0.244$, average precision of $0.505$, Hausdorff distance of $25.45\pm15.63$ mm, mean average surface distance of $9.40\pm8.49$ mm, and normalized surface distance of $0.355\pm0.236$, providing the best overlap and surface-distance performance among the evaluated unsupervised methods and Dice performance comparable to supervised ADC-only models. Optional population-derived ADC $Z$-map refinement further increased Dice to $0.602\pm0.269$. These findings support pathology-informed score discrepancies as a useful signal for neonatal HIE lesion localization, while highlighting remaining challenges in detecting small and low-contrast lesions.

title: Reading the Mask: Descriptor-Grounded BI-RADS Rationale Generation for Breast MRI Segmentation
abstract: Deep learning based models accurately delineate tumours on dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI), but segmentation masks alone do not provide the rationales or reasoning used by radiologists to assess the lesion suspicion. This limits the explainability as well the clinical integration. We investigate whether clinically relevant descriptors can instead be derived from the segmentation masks and their dynamic contrast-enhancement series. We have used Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (BI-RADS) guidelines as a structured framework. Using these guidelines we designed a BI-RADS decision tree with eight quantitative measurements using radiomics, together with the lesion size and component count, that determine the descriptors at eight nodes. Using these descriptors we generate natural-language rationale using a large language model. The model was constrained to express only the derived records from the decision tree. After applying this framework to the expert and automatic masks of each of the 1,506 cases in the MAMA-MIA dataset, we generated a reproducible corpus of 3,012 BI-RADS grounded rationales. We obtained a faithfulness score of 99.98% and a counterfactual accuracy of 99.3%, indicating that the generated rationales faithfully verbalises the measured descriptors and correctly reflects changes in the underlying record. Agreement between the descriptors from expert and automatic masks falls from 0.832 to 0.549 as mask quality falls from Good to Missed. The generated rationales are intended as draft representations for radiologist review and final sign-off rather than autonomous clinical reports.

title: An interpretable deep learning method for early hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis on multiphase CT
abstract: Early diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma is critical to preserve access to curative treatment options. The Liver Imaging Reporting and Data System (LI-RADS) provides a standardized framework for non-invasive diagnosis on multiphase computed tomography, based on major visual imaging features. However, these features may be difficult to assess consistently, particularly in small liver lesions. We developed dLI-RADS, an interpretable artificial intelligence method designed to estimate the probability of hepatocellular carcinoma from multiphase computed tomography images of manually segmented liver lesions, while remaining aligned with LI-RADS-related imaging concepts. dLI-RADS combines neural network-derived predictions with handcrafted quantitative imaging measurements reflecting LI-RADS major features and integrates these inputs using logistic regression. In this multicenter retrospective study, patients with multiphase computed tomography and at least one liver lesion were included, while lesions larger than 40 mm were excluded. Histology served as the reference standard for hepatocellular carcinoma, and a composite reference standard was used for non-hepatocellular carcinoma lesions. The lesion-level accuracy of dLI-RADS and LI-RADS were compared on the internal evaluation set using 10,000-repetition bootstrap non-inferiority tests, with 5% margins and significance levels. On the external test set, sensitivities were similarly compared. dLI-RADS was non-inferior to LI-RADS for lesion-level accuracy in the internal evaluation set, achieving 80% accuracy compared with 74% for LI-RADS (p = 0.04)...

title: Reference Manual of MEDiml
abstract: Radiomics is the high-throughput extraction of quantitative features (e.g., tumor shape, intensity distributions, and texture) from medical images to characterize tissues and uncover disease patterns invisible to the human eye. These features can serve as candidate imaging biomarkers for cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and classification. However, extracting thousands of features makes it difficult to identify the most informative ones for a given clinical task, while implementing an end-to-end workflow can require programming expertise that limits accessibility for clinical researchers. Hence, we propose MEDiml, an open-source, standards-compliant radiomics platform connecting feature extraction, predictive modeling, and interpretation through complementary graphical and programmatic interfaces. MEDiml combines a Python package (MEDiml-pkg) with a graphical desktop application (MEDiml-app) that enables researchers to conduct experiments without writing code. Both interfaces use the same computational implementation, and code generation exports graphically configured workflows as executable Python code, facilitating reproducibility and collaboration between clinical researchers and computational scientists. A typical MEDiml workflow includes image preprocessing, radiomic feature extraction, feature set reduction, model training and evaluation, and interpretation using feature importance. Feature sets can be grouped into levels of radiomic complexity (morphological, intensity-based, textural, and filter-based) to evaluate whether more complex features provide additional predictive value. This reference manual documents the radiomics concepts, workflow, software components, architecture, and installation, compares MEDiml with existing tools, and demonstrates its complexity-driven workflow on five oncological imaging cohorts comprising 2,104 patients. Resources: www.mediml.app.

title: Learning to Measure and Diagnose: A Clinical-Dictionary Radiomic Bottleneck Model for Thyroid Nodule Classification
abstract: Thyroid ultrasound supports the assessment of nodule malignancy, but classification predictions often lack evidence linked to familiar clinical descriptions. Radiomics provides explicitly defined measurements that can support such explanations through a clinical dictionary. However, using these measurements as interpretable evidence requires reliable estimation from ultrasound images and preservation of measurement fidelity when optimizing classification performance. We propose a clinical-dictionary radiomic bottleneck model for thyroid nodule classification. Within this model, Family-Aware Radiomic Learning (FARL) estimates measurements with balanced supervision across feature families. Fidelity-Guided Bottleneck Modeling (FGBM) constructs a fixed bottleneck, followed by joint optimization of measurement estimation and classification under fidelity guidance. Decision evidence decomposition then traces feature contributions through a linear classifier and organizes them by clinical dictionary categories. Experiments on ThyroidXL and TN3K show competitive classification performance, while case studies illustrate feature contributions for benign and malignant nodules. These findings indicate interpretable classification with inspectable quantitative evidence informed by clinical knowledge. Code is available online.

title: Controlling Variability in~Neuroimaging Analysis Pipelines with~Software Product Lines
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an acquisition technique used for medical diagnosis. It is notably used for structural and functional MRI (or fMRI) image analysis. MRI data is known to be complex and noisy, so pipelines are created to extract and enhance relevant information in retrieved images. The NARPS study highlighted the significant variability that can emerge from different pipelines set up by independent teams while trying to answer the same research question about brain functioning. Having different implementations realizing the same task is a typical playground for software product lines (SPLs), which may be out of the sight of neuroimage practitioners. Thus, proposing an SPL out of these different pipelines falls back on a typical reverse-engineering problem with its usual difficulties. In this document, we advocate for the conceptual adoption of SPL principles as a promising direction to improve reproducibility and consistency in neuroimaging research.

title: Expandable Modality Experts for Medical Vision-Language Learning
abstract: Learning across medical imaging modalities requires making use of images without paired text and accommodating new domains while retaining existing representations. We propose a medical vision-language technique built around an expandable bank of modality experts. Its Multiway Transformer combines shared visual computation with deterministically routed feed-forward experts and a separate text pathway. A modality-aware visual tokenizer supplies targets for masked pretraining on 19.4 million unpaired image rows across seven modalities; contrastive alignment then uses 3.23 million image-text pairs. Additional fundus and optical coherence tomography experts learn from paired data while the original image and text embedding paths remain frozen. With a ViT-Large backbone, the proposed technique achieves the best or tied-best result in 24 of 25 benchmark settings across nine modalities: 10 of 11 zero-shot classification benchmarks, all 10 linear probes, and all four retrieval benchmarks. Mean balanced accuracy is 0.674 for zero-shot classification and 0.856 for linear probing, and mean bidirectional retrieval recall is 20.70%. A separate three-seed sequential experiment with matched adaptation data yields fundus and OCT retrieval gains of 14.95 and 9.31 percentage points, with no measured loss on preceding fundus or pathology tasks. The preservation argument requires unchanged existing computation paths and inference conditions, and feature-identity checks verify retention on evaluated inputs. The proposed technique provides a modular approach to learning and expanding medical vision-language representations.

title: ViBMR: A Large-Scale Multi-Sequence Brain MRI Dataset and Comprehensive Evaluation for Vietnamese Radiology Report Generation
abstract: Automated radiology report generation for multi-sequence brain MRI holds strong promise for alleviating radiologists' workload, yet it remains a demanding problem: brain MRI studies are inherently volumetric, each pulse sequence carries complementary diagnostic information, and annotated data are critically scarce for low-resource clinical languages. Existing brain MRI-report resources are still dominated by English reports, translated clinical text, or datasets adapted from task-specific imaging benchmarks, leaving routine low-resource clinical reporting and heterogeneous multi-sequence MRI protocols insufficiently represented. To bridge this gap, we introduce ViBMR, to the best of our knowledge, the first large-scale multi-sequence brain MRI dataset paired with routine Vietnamese clinical reports, comprising 3,649 patients and 11,875 MRI series across T1, T2, FLAIR, and contrast-enhanced T1 sequences. Building on ViBMR, we establish a comprehensive evaluation setup for brain MRI report generation, covering representative medical vision-language models, multi-sequence inputs, and feature aggregation strategies. The results provide key insights into dataset characteristics and model behavior, while demonstrating the necessity of native low-resource clinical datasets for reliable Vietnamese-origin brain MRI report generation. Our dataset and baseline models will be released for non-commercial research.

title: A Contrastive Learning Framework for Label-Efficient Gastric Cancer Detection and Intra-Tumour Progression Analysis
abstract: Gastric Cancer is among the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide. The complexity and variability of histopathological images pose significant challenges for both pathologists and computer-based diagnostics, creating a growing need for machine learning approaches capable of capturing meaningful representations from limited labelled data. Selfsupervised Contrastive Learning (CL) has demonstrated promising results in natural image analysis; however, its application to gastric cancer histopathology remains underexplored. This paper proposes an integrated CL framework built on a ResNet50 encoder trained under the NT-Xent objective, without reliance on ImageNet pre-training, to learn discriminative and staining-invariant representations from H&E-stained tissue patches. The learned embeddings are transferred to a supervised downstream classifier for binary tumour/normal (TUM/NOR) detection, achieving a test accuracy of 83.13%, an AUC-ROC of 0.9087, and an Average Precision of 0.9063 - competitive with recent supervised and weakly-supervised approaches on comparable histopathology benchmarks. Beyond binary diagnosis, the framework applies K-Means clustering to tumour embeddings to identify four geometrically separable pseudo-stage clusters, confirmed by a Random Forest classifier achieving 97% accuracy and a mean Dice coefficient of 0.97, demonstrating the capacity of CL representations to encode progression-relevant morphological variation without stage-level annotations. Grad-CAM explainability is integrated throughout to ensure model transparency. The complete system is deployed via a Streamlit clinical interface. Compared to recent state-of-the-art methods the proposed framework operates with substantially fewer labelled samples while additionally providing unsupervised progression stratification and interpretable outputs, addressing a gap not covered by existing approaches.

title: Association of pre-closure intraoperative fibrinogen administration with early postoperative hemostasis in patients undergoing head-pelvic ring traction and three-column osteotomy for severe spinal deformity: a retrospective study.
abstract: Background Severe spinal deformity correction is associated with substantial perioperative blood loss. Evidence on pre-closure intraoperative fibrinogen administration in this setting remains limited. This study evaluated whether pre-closure intraoperative fibrinogen administration was associated with more favorable early postoperative hemostasis-related parameters. Methods This single-center retrospective study included 50 patients with severe spinal deformity who underwent head-pelvic ring traction followed by corrective surgery. Patients were classified into a fibrinogen group and a non-fibrinogen group according to whether they received pre-closure intraoperative fibrinogen administration. Postoperative coagulation parameters, hemoglobin (Hb) levels, drainage volume, and radiographic correction outcomes were compared between groups. Results Twenty-five patients were included in each group. Baseline characteristics, operative time, intraoperative blood loss, and radiographic correction outcomes were comparable between groups. Compared with the non-fibrinogen group, the fibrinogen group had lower postoperative prothrombin time and international normalized ratio, and higher prothrombin activity and fibrinogen levels (all P < 0.01). Hb levels on postoperative days 1 and 3 were higher in the fibrinogen group, whereas postoperative drainage volume and postoperative red blood cell transfusion volume were lower (P = 0.002, 0.036, 0.005, and < 0.001, respectively). No significant between-group difference was observed in Hb level on postoperative day 7. Conclusions Pre-closure intraoperative fibrinogen administration was associated with more favorable early postoperative hemostasis-related parameters in patients undergoing corrective surgery for severe spinal deformity. Given the retrospective design and potential residual confounding, these findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating and require validation in prospective studies.

title: Carbon nanotube-induced magnetic shielding effects on <sup>129</sup>Xe NMR from equivariant neural networks.
abstract: Equivariant graph neural networks (EGNNs) have been successfully used in building efficient and accurate machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for molecular dynamics (MD) and to predict nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) parameters in complex systems. In this work, EGNNs are used to fine-tune an atomistic foundation model, which serves as an MLIP for large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of xenon in carbon nanotubes. In addition, EGNNs are employed to develop a machine-learning model for the 129 Xe NMR magnetic shielding tensor, σ , enabling its direct prediction from the MLMD snapshots. Both models are data-efficient and remain accurate well beyond their training data. Using this dual-model framework, we show that xenon encapsulated in carbon nanotubes experiences a nanotube-induced, negative 129 Xe isotropic chemical shift that varies non-monotonically with nanotube diameter and depends further on temperature and Xe loading, establishing this dual-model approach as an efficient route to interpret confinement-driven 129 Xe NMR response.

title: Temporal trends in incidence, clinical characteristics and outcomes of pyogenic vertebral osteomyelitis in Southern Denmark from 2009 to 2022: a retrospective population-based cohort study.
abstract: Objectives Pyogenic vertebral osteomyelitis (PVO) is a severe infection with increasing incidence. We aimed to describe long-term population-based temporal trends in incidence, clinical presentation, diagnostic approaches, microbiology, and outcomes. Materials and methods We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study including 1,017 adults with multidisciplinary team-verified PVO diagnosed at a tertiary infectious diseases referral centre in the Region of Southern Denmark between 2009 and 2022. Incidence rates (IRs) per 100,000 person-years (PY) were calculated using regional population data and compared across three calendar periods (2009-2013, 2014-2018, 2019-2022). Temporal changes in clinical characteristics, microbiology, diagnostic strategies, and outcomes were assessed. Results In total, 1,017 patients were included. The crude IR increased from 4.7 per 100,000 PY in 2009-2013 to 11.0 in 2019-2022, with the largest increase among patients aged ≥70 years. Mean age and comorbidity burden rose over time. Pain was common, fever was often absent, and neurological deficits occurred in 33.5% ( n = 341). Postsurgical infection was the most frequent primary focus, and concomitant endocarditis occurred in 8.3% ( n = 84). A microbiological diagnosis was established in 64.8% ( n = 635) of cases, most commonly Staphylococcus aureus . Use of Fluorine-18 Fluorodeoxyglucose Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography ([ 18 F]FDG-PET/CT) increased over time. Median hospital stay remained 33 days. One-year mortality increased from 9.5% to 18.2%, while relapse declined, resulting in a stable composite risk of death or relapse (20.7%). Conclusions The incidence of PVO increased markedly from 2009 to 2022, predominantly in older patients with comorbidities. Despite improved diagnostics, microbiologically-negative cases remain frequent. Mortality remained high and increased over time.

title: Diagnostic Performance of the Radiographic Assessment of Lung Edema Score for Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome-Post Hoc Analysis of the "Validating Acute Lung Injury Biomarkers for Diagnosis" Study.
abstract: Objectives To determine the diagnostic accuracy of the Radiographic Assessment of Lung Edema (RALE) score for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and its interobserver reliability. Design Post hoc analysis of a prospective observational cohort study. Setting ICUs at Vanderbilt University Medical Center participating in the Validating Acute Lung Injury Biomarkers for Diagnosis study. Patients Adult patients receiving invasive ventilation for at least two consecutive days, with chest radiographs available on the first 2 ICU days. Interventions None. Measurements and main results Chest radiographs from the first 2 ICU days were scored independently by at least two experienced raters; scores were averaged per radiograph, and the highest averaged score from ICU day 1 or 2 was selected for analysis. The primary outcome was ARDS according to the Berlin definition during the first 2 ICU days. Of 236 patients, 92 (39%) had ARDS. The median RALE score was higher in patients with ARDS than in those without (29.5 [22.2-34.5] vs. 12.2 [7.5-17.8]; p < 0.01). The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.93 (95% CI, 0.90-0.96). At the optimal cutoff of 20, sensitivity was 85%, specificity 83%, positive predictive value 76%, and negative predictive value 90%. Interobserver reliability was high, with pairwise intraclass correlation coefficients ranging from 0.81 to 0.87. Conclusions In patients invasively ventilated for at least 2 days, the RALE score demonstrated excellent diagnostic accuracy for ARDS at a cutoff of 20, together with high interobserver reliability, supporting its potential role as a standardized radiographic tool in the diagnosis of ARDS.

title: Parasitic Infections of the Lacrimal System: A Major Review of Etiology, Clinical Presentation, and Management.
abstract: Purpose Parasitic infections of the lacrimal system are rare and often under-recognized causes of lacrimal pathology. Their clinical presentation frequently mimics more common conditions such as chronic dacryocystitis, leading to diagnostic challenges and delays in appropriate management. This study aims to systematically review the literature on parasitic infections of the lacrimal system and to characterize their etiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic approaches, management strategies, and outcomes. Methods A systematic review was conducted across MEDLINE, Embase, Emcare, and PubMed from inception to March 2026. Studies reporting parasitic infections involving the lacrimal apparatus were included. Data on demographics, clinical presentation, anatomical involvement, causative organisms, diagnostic methods, treatment, and outcomes were extracted. Due to heterogeneity and predominance of case reports and small series, a qualitative descriptive analysis was performed. Results A total of 44 studies comprising 172 cases were included. Rhinosporidium seeberi was the most frequently reported pathogen, accounting for 147 cases (85.5%), followed by Leishmania (8 cases, 4.7%) and Ascaris lumbricoides (7 cases, 4.1%). The lacrimal sac was the most commonly involved site. Clinical presentation was nonspecific, with epiphora and medial canthal swelling predominating. Diagnosis was most often established by histopathology following surgical intervention. Management varied by etiology, with surgical excision commonly used for rhinosporidiosis and mechanical extraction for helminthic infections. Outcomes were generally favorable, although recurrence was reported, particularly in R. seeberi infections. Conclusions Parasitic infections of the lacrimal system are rare but clinically important, with diverse presentations and management approaches. Increased awareness is essential for early diagnosis and appropriate treatment. Further studies with standardized reporting are needed to optimize management strategies.

title: Lactation Management in Patients With Cancer: An Evidence-Based Framework for Surgical Practice.
abstract: BackgroundThe coexistence of lactation and cancer care, termed oncolactation , is becoming increasingly common as childbearing is delayed and more women are diagnosed with malignancy during the reproductive years. However, evidence-based guidance regarding breastfeeding during oncologic evaluation and treatment remains fragmented, particularly for surgeons involved in multidisciplinary cancer care.MethodsWe conducted a narrative review with a systematic literature search using PubMed/MEDLINE and professional society guidelines (American Society of Breast Surgeons (ASBrS), American College of Radiology (ACR), American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), and the Drugs and Lactation Database (LactMed®). Publications addressing surgical management, diagnostic imaging, systemic therapy, radiation therapy, and reproductive counseling in lactating patients with cancer were critically synthesized to develop practical, evidence-based recommendations.ResultsMost diagnostic and surgical interventions-including mammography, breast MRI, computed tomography, image-guided biopsy, and general anesthesia-are compatible with continued breastfeeding when appropriate precautions are observed. Cytotoxic chemotherapy, endocrine therapy, and most targeted or immunotherapeutic agents remain contraindicated because of insufficient safety data or potential infant toxicity. Radiation therapy generally precludes breastfeeding from the treated breast, but permits continued feeding from the contralateral breast. Emerging evidence also supports individualized counseling regarding fertility preservation, future pregnancy, and survivorship.ConclusionsOncolactation should be incorporated into routine surgical oncology practice. Most surgical and diagnostic procedures can be performed without interrupting breastfeeding, whereas systemic therapies require individualized pharmacologic assessment. Integration of evidence-based lactation guidance into multidisciplinary cancer care promotes safe, patient-centered decision-making while maintaining oncologic safety and supporting breastfeeding whenever feasible.

title: Symptomatic Superior Vena Cava Lipoma Causing Near-Complete Venous Obstruction: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: BackgroundLipomas are common benign mesenchymal tumors; however, intravascular localization is exceedingly rare. Superior vena cava (SVC) involvement represents an exceptional entity, with only a limited number of cases reported in the literature. Intravascular lipomas are frequently detected incidentally but may present with symptoms related to venous obstruction, including superior vena cava syndrome. We report a rare case of SVC-origin intravascular lipoma extending into the right brachiocephalic vein, accompanied by a focused review of previously published upper extremity cases.Case PresentationA 77-year-old male presented with facial and cervical edema, dyspnea exacerbated in the supine position, and distended cervical veins. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed a 5-cm elongated, fat-attenuation mass within the SVC extending into the right brachiocephalic vein, causing near-total (approximately 99%) luminal occlusion. Transthoracic echocardiography supported the diagnosis. The patient underwent surgical resection via median sternotomy under cardiopulmonary bypass. Following longitudinal venotomy of the SVC extending to the brachiocephalic vein, the tumor-adherent to the posterior venous wall-was completely excised with preservation of vascular integrity. Primary venous repair was performed. The diagnosis of lipoma was histopathologically confirmed. The patient initially showed marked symptomatic improvement; however, on postoperative day 5, sudden-onset dyspnea necessitated reintubation, followed by multiorgan failure and death. The precise cause of the acute deterioration could not be definitively established.Literature review identified only 21 previously reported upper extremity intravenous lipomas, with this case representing the 16th involving the SVC and the oldest reported patient.ConclusionUpper extremity intravenous lipomas are rare and may lead to significant venous obstruction. Cross-sectional imaging is essential for diagnosis and surgical planning. In symptomatic patients, complete surgical excision provides definitive treatment and symptom relief. Management of incidentally detected asymptomatic cases remains controversial and should be individualized.

title: Why clinicians in acute hospitals may fail to engage in direct communication with people with intellectual disability.
abstract: This case highlights the healthcare inequities faced by people with intellectual disability, including diagnostic overshadowing, communication barriers, and the need for personalised, meaningful adjustments in care. A woman in her fifties with mild intellectual disability, epilepsy, and diabetes insipidus experienced delayed diagnosis and treatment because healthcare providers assumed she could not tolerate magnetic resonance imaging; however, when the scan was eventually completed with supported communication, it revealed a serious brain tumour with metastases. The case shows that diagnostic overshadowing can arise not only from misattributing symptoms, but also from untested assumptions about a patient's ability to engage with diagnostic procedures. It also underscores the importance of involving patients and families directly in healthcare decisions to support autonomy and prevent avoidable harm. Addressing these systemic issues is essential to deliver equitable, patient-centred care in acute hospital settings.

title: Computed tomography angiography with three-dimensional reconstruction for planning aortic valve replacement via right anterior mini-thoracotomy.
abstract: Introduction This study explored the value of computed tomography angiography (CTA) with three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction in aortic valve replacement (AVR) via right anterior mini-thoracotomy. Methods Clinical data were retrospectively collected from 168 patients who underwent AVR at our institution in China between 1 July 2018 and 1 September 2022. After 1:1 propensity score matching, the experimental group (right anterior mini-thoracotomy) and control group (median sternotomy) each comprised 43 patients. Patients in the experimental group underwent preoperative aortic CTA with 3D reconstruction to guide individualised selection of the intercostal incision site. Perioperative and clinical outcomes were compared between groups. Results The experimental group had significantly lower 24-hour postoperative drainage volume and shorter mechanical ventilation time, intensive care unit stay, and total hospital stay than the control group (all P<0.001). No intraoperative conversion to median sternotomy or postoperative reoperation for bleeding or pericardial tamponade occurred in the experimental group. Postoperatively, five patients (11.6%) developed atelectasis or pulmonary infection, five (11.6%) developed pleural effusion, and five (11.6%) developed subcutaneous emphysema or pneumothorax; none required thoracentesis. Aortic cross-clamping and cardiopulmonary bypass times were approximately 8 minutes longer, respectively, in the experimental group. At 24 months, the incidence of the composite endpoint-including all-cause mortality, cardiocerebrovascular complications, and readmission for massive pleural effusion or coagulation dysfunction-did not differ significantly between groups. Conclusion Preoperative CTA with 3D reconstruction enables accurate localisation of the right intercostal incision for AVR via right anterior mini-thoracotomy. This technique preserves minimally invasive surgery benefits and does not increase risks of mid/long-term adverse events.

At 24 months, the incidence of the composite endpoint-including all-cause mortality, cardiocerebrovascular complications, and readmission for massive pleural effusion or coagulation dysfunction-did not differ significantly between groups.

Conclusion

Preoperative CTA with 3D reconstruction enables accurate localisation of the right intercostal incision for AVR via right anterior mini-thoracotomy. This technique preserves minimally invasive surgery benefits and does not increase risks of mid/long-term adverse events.

title: Brain Tumour Detection Using EfficientNet-Transformer Hybrid Network with SHAP and Grad-CAM Based Explainable Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Accurate and interpretable brain tumour detection from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains a significant challenge in computer-aided diagnosis. This study proposes an EfficientNet–Transformer Hybrid Network integrated with SHapley Additive ExPlanations (SHAP) and Grad-CAM explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques for automated and trustworthy brain tumour classification. Methods: The proposed framework combines EfficientNet for local feature extraction and a Vision Transformer for global contextual learning. MRI images from publicly available benchmark datasets containing four classes (glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumour, and no tumour) were preprocessed and augmented before training. The model was trained using an 80:20 training-testing split, while SHAP and Grad-CAM were employed to provide feature-level and spatial explanations of predictions. Results: The proposed framework achieved a classification accuracy of 98.88%, outperforming several state-of-the-art CNN and transformer models. It also attained average precision, recall, and F1-score values of 98.90%, 98.88%, and 98.89%, respectively, with an average AUC of 0.9893. Ablation and robustness analyses demonstrated that integrating SHAP and Grad-CAM improved interpretability while maintaining high predictive performance under noisy conditions. Conclusions: The proposed EfficientNet–Transformer framework effectively combines local and global feature learning with dual explainability mechanisms to deliver accurate and clinically interpretable brain tumour classification. The results demonstrate its potential as a reliable computer-aided diagnosis tool for neuro-oncology and clinical decision support systems.

title: Beyond the Classical Paradigm of Diabetic Kidney Disease (DKD): Evolving Phenotypes and the Role of Kidney Biopsy
abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is increasingly recognized as a heterogeneous condition encompassing distinct clinical and pathological phenotypes. Albuminuria and estimated glomerular filtration rate may follow divergent trajectories, with non-albuminuric kidney function decline representing a common and clinically relevant phenotype. Importantly, clinical features do not always reflect the underlying renal pathology, as patients with diabetes may present with diabetic kidney disease, non-diabetic kidney disease (NDKD), or mixed lesions. Conventional clinical markers, including diabetic retinopathy, hematuria, proteinuria, and eGFR decline, modify but do not reliably establish the underlying diagnosis. Kidney biopsy therefore retains a selective but important role in patients with atypical or rapidly evolving presentations, particularly when histological findings may alter treatment or prognosis. Beyond diagnostic classification, biopsy can provide prognostic information through assessment of glomerular, tubulointerstitial, and vascular injury. Future approaches should integrate longitudinal clinical trajectories with histopathology and molecular profiling, positioning kidney biopsy as a bridge toward mechanism-based classification and precision medicine in DKD.

title: Binary Classification of Breast Cancer Images Using CNNs Enhanced by ALO-CLAHE-MSER Preprocessing
abstract: This work presents an intelligent image-processing framework for automatically detecting and clas-sifying benign and malignant regions in breast tissue by integrating Contrast Limited Adaptive His-togram Equalization (CLAHE), Maximally Stable Extremal Regions (MSER), and metaheuristic opti-mization algorithms. Identifying tumor-related regions in breast images is challenging because their visual characteristics can vary considerably with tissue density, illumination conditions, surface tex-ture, intensity distribution, lesion severity, and image acquisition conditions. These variations can make conventional image segmentation and manually configured MSER approaches sensitive to pa-rameter selection and less robust when detecting heterogeneous cancerous regions. To address these limitations, this study highlights the critical role of metaheuristic optimization as a key driver for fully automating and optimizing the combined CLAHE-MSER pipeline for binary breast cancer classifica-tion. Methods: First, CLAHE is applied to the input medical images to improve local contrast and enhance visual differences between healthy and cancerous tissue. The enhanced images are subse-quently processed using the MSER technique to identify stable intensity regions potentially associated with lesions or tumor masses. Rather than relying on manual configuration, the MSER parameter space and enhancement thresholds are formulated as a multidimensional optimization problem, and metaheuristic optimization algorithms are employed to automatically explore the parameter space and determine optimal configurations for region detection. Candidate solutions are iteratively evalu-ated using an objective function designed to improve the quality, stability, spatial coherence, and ac-curacy of the detected tumor regions prior to binary classification. The proposed metaheuristic-driven CLAHE-MSER framework therefore lets the detection process adapt automatically to the visual char-acteristics of individual medical images while eliminating dependence on manually selected parame-ters. Results: We performed experimental evaluations on medical images containing healthy, benign, and malignant regions. We quantitatively evaluated the performance of the proposed CLAHE-MSER framework, optimized by metaheuristic algorithms, using several image-quality, region-detection, and binary classification metrics. The experimental results indicate that incorporating CLAHE improves local contrast and facilitates the identification of subtle differences between healthy and affected tis-sue. Furthermore, metaheuristic optimization significantly improves MSER parameter selection, re-sulting in more consistent and spatially coherent detection of tumor regions than conventional MSER configurations and non-optimized approaches. The optimized configurations better preserve relevant cancer-related structures, maximizing overall binary classification accuracy while drastically reduc-ing the detection of healthy tissue and irrelevant regions. Conclusion: Integrating CLAHE- MSER, and metaheuristic optimization provides a robust, fully automated, and adaptive framework for binary breast cancer classification based on medical image analysis. CLAHE enhances the visual infor-mation needed to distinguish affected tissue, while MSER extracts stable image regions associated with potential tumor lesions. Metaheuristic optimization serves as the central component to automate and refine the detection process by dynamically identifying suitable parameter configurations for different image conditions. The proposed methodology represents a promising computational ap-proach for automated breast cancer screening, computer-aided diagnosis (CAD), lesion classification, and intelligent medical decision support systems.

title: A Systematic Review and Descriptive Quantitative Synthesis of Artificial Intelligence in Cervical Cancer Screening and Diagnosis
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) has been frequently utilised in cervical cancer screening, diagnosis, lesion assessment and clinical decision support, but the evidence remains methodologically heterogeneous. This systematic review examined the application of AI in cytology, colposcopy, visual examination, histopathology, and multimodal clinical data. Also reviewed PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and IEEE Xplore to identify 4094 records. After the exclusion of 2053 duplicates and applying pre-defined eligibility criteria, 898 studies were included. Directly extractable diagnostic-performance measures were available from 60 studies. Accuracy was reported in 40 studies, sensitivity in 19, specificity in 16 and AUC in 12 studies. A total of 13 studies reported both sensitivity and specificity. There was considerable heterogeneity in populations, datasets, reference standards, diagnostic tasks, AI methods, validation procedures and performance reporting. Complete TP, FP, TN and FN data were not available across the eligible evidence base and pooled diagnostic accuracy estimation and summary receiver-operating-characteristic analysis were not possible. Therefore, the quantitative results were summarized descriptively. Evidence indicates broad application of AI approaches but also limitations in terms of comparability, external validation, reporting completeness and clinical generalizability. Future research should focus on standardized reporting, multicenter datasets, independent external validation and prospective clinical evaluation.

title: An acoustic coupling fluid improves intraoperative ultrasound image quality during glioma surgery: Results of a Pivotal Multicenter Study (NCT04734444)
abstract: Abstract Intraoperative ultrasound uniquely provides repeatable, real-time guidance throughout glioma resection without interrupting surgery. However, image quality deteriorates at resection completion, when imaging is most critical: irrigation fluids attenuate ultrasound less than brain tissue, producing hyperechoic artefacts beneath the cavity that obscure or mimic residual tumour. Existing operator-dependent strategies do not correct this mismatch. Here, we show that SonoClear, a tissue-mimicking acoustic coupling fluid, reduces these artefacts and improves interpretability. In a prospective, non-randomised study at five centres, 44 patients received SonoClear and 40 contributed to paired comparisons with standard irrigation fluid. SonoClear reduced below-cavity artefactual signal (ratio of contrast-to-noise ratios, irrigation/SonoClear: 1.70; 95% CI, 1.48–1.95). Five independent neurosurgeons masked to the fluid reported a mean paired Surgeon Image Rating improvement of 1.96 points (95% CI, 1.80–2.11). No serious adverse events were judged probably or definitely device-related within 30 days; postoperative magnetic resonance imaging showed no major findings in 36 evaluated patients. These findings support acoustic matching to improve ultrasound guidance, including at resection completion; effects on resection extent and patient outcomes require investigation.

title: Successful emicizumab prophylaxis in treatment-refractory acquired von Willebrand syndrome associated with rheumatoid arthritis
abstract: Abstract Acquired von Willebrand syndrome (AVWS) is a rare bleeding disorder characterized by acquired quantitative or qualitative abnormalities of von Willebrand factor (VWF) and may occur in association with autoimmune disease. Management can be challenging when conventional hemostatic and immunomodulatory therapies fail. We report a 63-year-old man with longstanding rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and no personal or family history of abnormal bleeding who developed life-threatening hemorrhage following dental extractions, resulting in airway obstruction requiring tracheostomy and red blood cell transfusion. Evaluation demonstrated an isolated prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time, markedly reduced factor VIII (FVIII) activity, profoundly decreased VWF antigen and activity, and no detectable FVIII inhibitor. The late onset of bleeding, negative genetic testing, poor VWF recovery following high-dose VWF/FVIII concentrate, and underlying autoimmune disease supported a diagnosis of AVWS. Severe VWF deficiency persisted despite treatment with rituximab, methotrexate, and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). Emicizumab was subsequently initiated for prophylactic hemostasis. The patient remained free of spontaneous bleeding despite persistent severe reductions in VWF and FVIII measurements and subsequently underwent upper endoscopy with biopsy and colonoscopy without hemorrhagic complications using adjunctive tranexamic acid. To our knowledge, this represents the first reported case of RA-associated AVWS successfully managed with emicizumab prophylaxis. This case demonstrates sustained clinical hemostasis with emicizumab in treatment-refractory AVWS associated with RA and supports further investigation of FVIII-mimetic therapy as a potential prophylactic strategy when conventional therapies are ineffective.

title: Synoptic procedural reporting to improve quality indicators in systematic Staging Endobronchial Ultrasound (EBUS) in Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC): protocol for an ambispective multi-centre quality improvement study
abstract: Abstract Background: Accurate mediastinal staging by systematic staging endobronchial ultrasound (EBUS) is essential for prognosticating and guiding management in curative-intent treatment in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Narrative procedural reports are often incomplete and inconsistent between clinicians, limiting assessment of procedural quality and meaningful audit. Synoptic (structured, check-list style) reporting has improved documentation completeness and procedural quality in other domains of medicine, and a recent Australian multicentre study demonstrated synoptic reporting significantly improved both report and procedural quality in staging EBUS. This ambispective, international, multicentre study aims to evaluate whether synoptic procedural reporting improves quality indicators of systematic staging EBUS, encompassing both process and outcome measures, and will assess acceptability and feasibility to proceduralists. Methods: This ambispective multicentre, single-arm interventional study will recruit approximately 15 lung cancer services with substantial EBUS procedural volume. Eligible patients will have known or suspected clinical stage IB-IIIC NSCLC undergoing systematic staging EBUS for treatment planning. Each centre will implement a mandated synoptic report requiring documentation for each of the five mediastinal lymph nodes: examination, size of node and biopsy details. Three months of staging procedures will be contributed prior to and following implementation of this reporting practice. The primary outcome is the proportion of patients with a complete staging procedure. Secondary outcomes include PET-occult lymph node metastases detection, nodes sampled, radiologically normal node sampling, inter-site variance, and proceduralist feasibility/acceptability. A sample of 590 patients (295 pre-, 295 post-intervention) provides 80% power to detect an 8% increase in complete staging. Mixed-effects logistic and Poisson regression, with random effect for centre and adjustment for pre-specified baseline case-mix covariates, will be used. Discussion: This study will provide the first international multicentre evaluation of whether synoptic reporting improves procedural completeness and clinically meaningful outcomes in systematic staging EBUS. Demonstrating improved complete staging procedures and PET-occult lymph node detection, with proceduralist acceptability, would support widespread adoption of synoptic reporting as a quality improvement tool, strengthen alignment with WABIP quality frameworks, reduce variance in care, and support more accurate multidisciplinary decision-making for NSCLC patients. Trial registration: Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ANZCTR), ACTRN12625001281482. Registered 18 November 2025. Retrospectively registered.

title: From detection to decision: radiographic predictors of clinical complications in 514 supernumerary teeth: A retrospective cross-sectional study
abstract: Abstract Background Supernumerary teeth exhibit various morphological characteristics and may lead to a range of complications. This study aimed to evaluate radiographic characteristics of supernumerary teeth in children and to determine associations with complications and treatment status. Materials and methods This study included 386 systemically healthy paediatric patients (5–15.9 years) with 514 supernumerary teeth identified on panoramic radiographs. Variables included number, location, morphology, eruption direction, eruption status, root development stage, and complications. Statistical analyses included chi-square tests, independent samples t-tests, and multivariable binary logistic and multinomial regression models. Results The mean age was 9.07 ± 2.08 years, and 70.2% of patients were male. Significant differences were observed between erupted and impacted teeth regarding morphology, eruption direction, root development stage, complications, and Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) use (p < 0.05). Morphology and root development stage were associated with complication patterns (p < 0.05). Multivariable regression analyses showed that CBCT use was associated with eruption status, dentition “stage, side distribution, and delayed eruption. Anterior maxillary localisation was strongly associated with conical and tuberculate morphologies. Midline location was associated with increased odds of both complete and partial root development (p < 0.001). Conclusion Supernumerary teeth exhibit distinct radiographic characteristics associated with clinical complications. Morphology, eruption status, and root development were associated with clinical and radiographic findings. Early radiographic evaluation is essential for individualised treatment planning.

title: Functional and MRI improvement followed by a mixed trajectory during cannabinoid-terpenoid exposure in glioblastoma: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background: Glioblastoma has limited salvage options, while viable tumour, treatment injury, postoperative change, oedema and corticosteroid effects may produce overlapping clinical and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings. Materials and Methods: Clinical records, serial MRI examinations and signed radiology reports were reviewed descriptively for a patient with IDH-wildtype, MGMT-promoter-methylated glioblastoma. The exposure history and contemporaneously documented neurological findings were aligned with seven MRI time points. No blinded central review, standardised volumetry or formal RANO 2.0 adjudication was performed. Results: After two operations, radiotherapy, concomitant temozolomide and three adjuvant cycles, serial MRI documented progression before April 2025. During a non-standard exposure state comprising intranasal perillyl alcohol and alpha-bisabolol, individualised cannabinoids and docosahexaenoic acid/medium-chain triglyceride oil, with dexamethasone fixed at 2 mg/day, hemiplegia/KPS 50 improved to hemiparesis with regained walking/KPS 80, coinciding with reduced enhancement. Later MRI showed increasing right temporal and cerebellar enhancement, including a new contralateral cerebellar focus, despite substantially stable postoperative cavity and T2/FLAIR extent. June 2026 lesion perfusion curves were low-amplitude without pathological hyperperfusion. The patient subsequently died after an overall survival of 45 months. Conclusions: This uncontrolled case documents early functional and radiological improvement on a stable corticosteroid background, followed by an anatomically progressive but biologically indeterminate trajectory. It does not establish treatment causality, survival benefit, formal tumour response or component-specific efficacy; mixed viable tumour and treatment effect or radiation necrosis could not be excluded. Although this single case does not establish a verified benefit the observed overall survival reached a time span of extraordinarily 45 months.

title: Neural correlates of empathy in autism: a coordinate-based meta-analysis
abstract: Abstract Purpose . Autistic and non-autistic people often differ in how readily they understand one another’s intentions and emotional states. Although empathy is commonly invoked to explain these differences, which components of empathic processing differ in autism, and their neural underpinnings, remain unclear. Methods . We conducted a pre-registered coordinate-based meta-analysis (activation likelihood estimation; ALE) of task-based fMRI studies of empathy in autism, examining within-group convergence, conjunction and between-group divergence separately for affective and cognitive components. title: Clinical and radiological comparisons of posterior labral tears with and without posterior glenohumeral instability.
abstract: Background We compare clinical and radiological characteristics and evaluate surgical outcomes of posterior labral tears based on the presence of glenohumeral instability. Methods Patients who were unresponsive to conservative treatment and underwent arthroscopic posterior labral repair were reviewed retrospectively. Patients were divided into two groups: those with glenohumeral instability (group 1) and those without (group 2). Demographic, radiological, physical examination, and intraoperative data were collected. Clinical outcomes were assessed at a minimum 2-year follow-up using the visual analog scale for pain, American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons, and Rowe scores. Results The study included a total of 85 patients (40 in group 1 and 45 in group 2) with a mean follow-up duration of 31.8±12.2 months. Patients in group 2 were older (31.4±1.0 years old, P<0.001), had longer symptom durations (30.1±5.6 months, P=0.002), and included fewer histories of trauma (16 patients, P=0.009). Competitive sports were more common in group 1 (9 patients, P=0.005), whereas weightlifting exercises were more common in group 2 (24 patients, P=0.047). Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) underestimated incomplete posterior labral tears more frequently in group 2 than in group 1 (P=0.033). The incidence of arthroscopically detected tears among MRI-occult tears was higher in group 2 (10 patients) than in group 1 (2 patients, P=0.029). Statistically significant improvements in shoulder function were observed postoperatively in both groups. Conclusions Clinical and magnetic resonance findings of posterior labral tears without glenohumeral instability differ from those with instability. Surgical treatment achieved satisfactory clinical outcomes regardless of the presence of instability. Level of evidence: III.

title: FreqFuseNet: Scale-Normalized Dual-Frequency Fusion for Thin-Wall Head-and-Neck OAR Segmentation
abstract: Accurate segmentation of thin-wall organs-at-risk (OARs) in head-and-neck computed tomography (CT) is challenging because small contour deviations can substantially affect boundary agreement. We present FreqFuseNet, a segmentation architecture with a fast Fourier transform (FFT) primary branch and a frequency channel attention network (FcaNet) residual branch that explicitly aligns heterogeneous frequency-feature scales before bounded residual fusion. An initialization-time analysis revealed an approximately 863-fold activation-scale disparity between the two branches, corresponding to an approximately 43-fold unintended residual-to-primary magnitude ratio under naive fusion with a nominal coefficient of 0.05. FreqFuseNet uses per-sample, per-channel scale alignment to preserve the intended relative amplitude without additional normalization parameters. We evaluated 10 thin-wall OARs on SegRap2023 (84 training, 18 validation, and 18 testing CT cases) under a standardized binary per-OAR region-of-interest (ROI) protocol. In two training seeds, FreqFuseNet achieved Dice of 0.849 and 0.843, 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) of 0.824 and 0.823 mm, and surface Dice at 1 mm of 0.959 and 0.957. In case-level paired comparisons for the primary seed (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, not corrected for multiple comparisons), FreqFuseNet showed significant improvements over 3D U-Net and MedNeXt-S, whereas differences versus an alternative learned fusion design (FixedFusion) and SegResNet were not statistically significant. These findings identify a practical feature-scale calibration issue in dual-frequency segmentation and demonstrate competitive boundary-sensitive performance of the proposed architecture within the evaluated ROI-based setting.

title: Distinct spatial organization of human hippocampal perfusion and microvascular pulsatility across age
abstract: Arterial pulsation can modulate neuronal activity through mechanosensitive pathways in mice, but whether vascular pulsatility is similarly related to neural organization in humans remains unclear. Here, using 7T MRI in 35 young and older adults, we mapped cerebral perfusion and microvascular volumetric pulsatility index (mvPI) across the unfolded hippocampus and integrated these measures with histological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic reference maps. Perfusion and mvPI exhibited distinct spatial organization and age-related differences. In young adults, perfusion preferentially corresponded to parvalbumin-interneuron density and beta/gamma distribution, whereas mvPI was associated with theta-band distribution. A number of associations detected in young adults were not detected in the older adults maps. Spectral simulations showed qualitative similarity to heartbeat-related phase resetting as one possible explanation for the mvPI-theta relationship, while spatial transcriptomics revealed perivascular enrichment of PIEZO2, a candidate mediator of vascular mechanotransduction. Together, these findings establish perfusion and tissue-level pulsatility as distinct dimensions of human hippocampal vascular organization and provide a framework for investigating their relationships with neural dynamics across aging.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Fine Needle Aspiration Cytology in Thyroid Diseases: Comparison with Histopathological Findings in Hawassa, Ethiopia
abstract: Introduction: Thyroid diseases are major health problems and among the most common endocrine disorders worldwide, including in Ethiopia. They are characterized by alterations in hormone secretion, enlargement of the thyroid gland, or both. Fine needle aspiration cytology is an important initial screening tool, and histopathologic examination is essential for the definitive diagnosis of thyroid disease. This study aimed to compare the diagnostic accuracy of fine needle aspiration cytology with histopathology in identifying thyroid diseases. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted at three health facilities in Hawassa City, Ethiopia, involving 304 patients who underwent both thyroid fine needle aspiration cytology and histopathologic examination of the same site between 30th October 2024 and 29th October 2025. FNAC results were classified using the Bethesda system, with histopathology as the gold standard. Data were entered into Kobo Toolbox, exported to SPSS version 27, and analyzed using cross-tabulation and chi-square (χ²) tests to determine diagnostic accuracy. Result: 304 patient records were included in the study. The fine needle aspiration cytology was determinate/diagnostic in 81.6% of cases. The study revealed the sensitivity and specificity of fine needle aspiration cytology to be 88.2% (CI 77.6-95.1%) and 94.4% (CI 90.6-97.1%), respectively. The false negative and false positive rates in this study were 2.4% and 4.4%, respectively. The positive predictive value was 80.3% (CI 68.7-89.3%), and the negative predictive value was 96.8% (CI 93.8-98.7%). The accuracy of fine needle aspiration cytology in differentiating benign from malignant thyroid lesions was 93.1%. Conclusion: FNAC demonstrated strong agreement with histopathology and remains a reliable, cost-effective first-line diagnostic tool for thyroid disease, particularly in resource-limited settings. Strengthening sample handling, ultrasound guidance, and adherence to Bethesda criteria may further improve diagnostic precision

title: Discrepancies in Interpretation of Japanese Radiology Report Expressions Between Radiologists and Referring Physicians
abstract: Objectives To evaluate discrepancies between radiologists and referring physicians in the interpretation of diagnostic probabilities conveyed by common Japanese expressions used in radiology reports. Materials and Methods Fifteen expressions commonly used to convey diagnostic probabilities in radiology reports were selected by five attending radiologists. An anonymous online survey was distributed to 26 radiologists and 33 referring physicians at a single institution. Participants assigned a diagnostic probability (from 0% to 100% in 10% increments) to each expression. Differences in median probabilities between radiologists and referring physicians were analyzed using the Mann-Whitney U test. Variability in interpretation was assessed using interquartile range (IQR), with IQR [≥] 30% defined as substantial variability. Results All radiologists (26/26) and 97% of referring physicians (32/33) completed the survey. Seven of the 15 expressions showed statistically significant differences in interpretation between radiologists and referring physicians: "c/w" (80% vs. 60%; p = 0.031), the Japanese equivalents of "present" (100% vs. 100%; p = 0.024), "suspect of" (80% vs. 70%; p = 0.007), "possibly" (50% vs. 70%; p < 0.001), "unlikely" (10% vs. 10%; p = 0.022), "cannot be ruled out" (25% vs. 40%; p < 0.001), and "not inconsistent with" (80% vs. 90%; p = 0.008). Substantial variability in interpretation (IQR [≥] 30%) was observed for four expressions: "cannot be ruled out" (IQR, 10%-40%), "s/o" (IQR, 60%-90%), "c/w" (IQR, 50%-90%), and "not inconsistent with" (IQR, 70%-100%). Conclusion This study revealed that nearly half of the Japanese expressions commonly used to convey diagnostic probabilities were interpreted differently by radiologists and referring physicians. These discrepancies highlight the need for a standardized lexicon to improve clarity and consistency in radiology reporting.
